thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a sharp latency/throughput cliff when the driver switched kernel for long sequences (>=1024). Dumping a quick profile now.
aj: Oof. Is this the post-driver-regen rollout? Any KV cache churn?
maria: Yes rollout at 2959126000. Quick paste of the top lines from the perf dump:
```
seq_len bucket: 256  -> kernel: fast-attn-v2, p50 18ms, kv_miss 2%
seq_len bucket: 1024 -> kernel: wide-attn-v1, p50 48ms, kv_miss 37%
batching: avg batch size fell from 12 -> 5 for long seqs
kv cache misses correlated with model reloads and driver handshake errors
```
sam: That kv_miss spike at 1024 looks like key namespace mismatch after the driver changed the salting scheme. Did the driver bump key version?
lee: I noticed the driver added an arch tag to the key schema earlier (arch=gpuv2) — new key format is: `model:ver:arch:seqlen_bin:session`. Old format was `model:ver:seqlen_bin:session`.
nina: If keys changed, the runtime would cold-start cache for those cohorts which explains smaller batch sizes and worse kernel packing. Did persistence write a migration?
maria: No migration — we expected backward-compatible lookup, but the lookup code uses exact key -> miss. So after regen, all running workers generated new keys.
aj: Can we hot-fix by falling back the driver to old keying, or make runtime accept both keys for 24h? Which is faster?
sam: Accepting both is safer but needs a tiny change in lookup path and a perf test. Quick hack: try ASN lookup fallback — probe new key, then old key, but short-circuit metrics. Risk: adds a conditional on hot path.
lee: Alternatively, we can persist a key-salting-mapping table in KV store (small) that maps new->old key salt for a grace period. That keeps hot path single lookup if we populate the mapping during driver handshake.
maria: For immediate mitigation, toggling kernel selection policy to prefer the older kernel for seqlen>=512 avoids the cliff — we saw p50 drop back to ~22ms in canary. But cost went up ~12%.
aj: Can we quantify kv_miss rate by seqlen? I propose adding metric `kv_miss_rate_by_seqlen` and an alert if >10% in any bin for 5m.
sam: I ran a small test: enabling dual-key lookup reduces miss from 37% -> 6% on synthetic replay (seqlen=1024) but adds ~1.4ms overhead avg. Numbers: p50 48ms -> 49.4ms, acceptable for short window.
nina: Nice. How about persistence — do we need to backfill persisted keys for older workers? RocksDB writer isn't uniform across runtimes.
lee: If we do mapping table approach, we must persist the mapping to the same store used by workers (local RocksDB + optional central metadata). Need a migration plan: populate mapping from driver at startup, invalidate after 48h.
maria: Also observed some kernel selector oddity: for long seqs it sometimes picks narrow-kernel due to stale sequence-length histograms per-worker. That interacts badly with cache misses because narrow kernel expects a denser KV layout. We should publish a driver handshake that pushes a fresh seqlen histogram to router during canary.
aj: So plan A (fast): enable dual-key lookup in runtime for 24h + metric + canary rollback flag. Plan B (medium): driver revert key-salting change and push migration. Plan C (correct): mapping table + handshake + kernel selector protection that prefers kernel pinned during cache warmup.
sam: I'll put up a PR for the dual-key fallback. Small change in kv/lookup.cpp: probe new_key then old_key, instrument counters.
nina: I'll coordinate canary (canary id: canary-2959129) and increase obs retention for kv metrics for 12h. Also tagging SRE. :eyes:
ops-bot: Alert created: KV_MISS_HIGH for eng-runtime (rule kv_miss_rate_by_seqlen > 10% in 5m) — link: https://alerts.internal/INC-8879
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: canary-2959129 -> 2959129800 (started)
lee: We should also add a deprecation header to logs so any future keying change includes an automated migration plan. Document the key format change in the driver release notes.
maria: Agreed. For follow-up: meeting 30m to validate PR perf, run synthetic replay, and finalize rollback if needed. Who can join?
aj: I'll be there.
sam: Me as well, will bring microbench numbers.
lee: I'll join and bring a patch for kernel selector tweak (pin for warmup).
nina: I'll handle canary monitoring and coordinate with SRE.
maria: Thanks all — I'll post the PR link and the replay job id before the meeting. :thumbsup:
